findings.title: Hash chain is not authentication: hostile remote can inject valid-hash human-actor events (consent, phase) via pull
findings.claim: ∃ remote R: syncPull(L,R) appends e with actor.kind=human ∧ e ∈ HUMAN_ONLY_EVENTS ∧ e never typed by the local human (verifyChain(L‖e) ok, fold ok)
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/cloud/sync.test.ts  (tests 'cannot inject a human-only DECISION_RECORDED...' and '...PHASE_CHANGED...'): fake client returns a doc whose event is DECISION_RECORDED/actor human with hash=computeEventHash(body); pull accepts it and hasGeminiConsent(state) becomes true.
findings.observed: RED: forged human DECISION_RECORDED appended to local events.jsonl; Gemini consent granted; PHASE_CHANGED from cloud applied. AI-actor forgery of human-only events IS rejected (green).
findings.fix: Sign events with a locally held key (or store per-device HMAC/ed25519 signatures) and require a valid signature on pull; or quarantine pulled HUMAN_ONLY events until the human re-confirms with a challenge code.

findings.title: Pull never checks that the delivered chain ends at the advertised meta head (headHash) and ignores event timestamps
findings.claim: ∃ remote: meta.headHash ≠ hash(last served event) ∧ syncPull succeeds; also ∃ event with at < previous.at appended
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/sync.test.ts: 'rejects a chain whose last hash differs from the meta head it advertised' and 'rejects events whose timestamps run backwards or into the far past' (event dated 1970 appended).
findings.observed: RED both: pull succeeded with meta head hash 'ffff...' and with an event at 1970-01-01. Truncated/short fetches (fewer docs than headSeq) are also accepted silently.
findings.fix: After the loop assert last.hash===remoteMeta.headHash && last.seq===remoteMeta.headSeq; enforce at monotonic; require fetched.length===headSeq-lastLocalSeq.

findings.title: Interrupted push wedges sync permanently: retry re-sets existing event docs, which rules forbid (update:false)
findings.claim: ∃ partial failure during pushEvents (events batches committed, meta batch not) ⇒ every later push throws PERMISSION_DENIED forever
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/sync.test.ts 'a push interrupted ... can be retried'; rule-level: tests/redteam/cloud/rules.test.ts 'push retry must be idempotent' (emulator: PERMISSION_DENIED ... false for 'update'). Cause: pushEvents writes meta only in the LAST 450-doc batch; retry recomputes toPush from stale meta and batch.set()s existing docs.
findings.observed: RED in both. Emulator: 'evaluation error at L76:26 for create, false for update'. Any log >450 events or any network drop mid-push hits this.
findings.fix: Make writes idempotent: allow update when request.resource.data == resource.data in rules; or read remote event docs before pushing; or write meta first as 'pending' then events.

findings.title: DefaultFirestoreSyncClient never authenticates: stored login is never used, every real request is anonymous and rejected by the rules
findings.claim: sync.ts imports no auth API and credentials.refreshToken is never read outside doctor/login; ∀ real push/pull: request.auth == null ⇒ denied
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/sync.test.ts 'DefaultFirestoreSyncClient authenticates the Firestore session' (greps for getAuth/signInWith/idToken in src/cloud/sync.ts; also hardcoded initializeApp({projectId:'cws-base'}) with no apiKey). Only the injected fake client has ever been exercised by tests/cloud/sync.test.ts.
findings.observed: RED: no auth usage. The feature 'cws sync' cannot work against real Firestore; its tests pass only because the client is mocked.
findings.fix: Exchange refresh token via Firebase Auth REST (securetoken) or firebase/auth signInWithCredential, configure from env/project config, and add an emulator-backed integration test.

findings.title: Rules are untested (tests/firebase/rules.test.ts is 0 bytes) and weak: no read-only dashboard, doc-id/seq mismatch, meta delete/rollback, no size or shape limits
findings.claim: I13 'dashboard is read-only' is unenforceable: allow write:if isOwner(uid) for projects, create for events, for ANY client of the same uid; events not bound to doc id; meta deletable and head rewritable
findings.witness: JAVA_HOME=C:\Users\takey\.local\tribunal\jdk\jdk-21.0.12.1+1; PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH; npx firebase emulators:exec --only firestore --project demo-cws-redteam "node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/cloud/rules.test.ts"
findings.observed: Emulator ran (JDK 21). Baseline GREEN: other uid read/list denied, unauth denied. RED (9/9): plain owner client can write events and meta, event id 000005 with seq 99 accepted, hash='not-a-hash' accepted, extra fields accepted, 300KB event accepted, meta delete accepted, headSeq rollback 50->1 accepted. 'npm run test:rules' runs an empty file and passes vacuously.
findings.fix: Gate writes on a CLI-only custom claim (request.auth.token.cws_writer==true); require seq==int(docId), hash.matches('^[0-9a-f]{64}$'), request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly([...]), size limits, meta create/update only with headSeq >= resource.data.headSeq, no meta delete; write real rules tests.

findings.title: Events are undeletable by their owner: secrets/PII pushed to Firestore can never be removed from the client
findings.claim: events/{seq}: allow delete,update: if false ⇒ ∀ owner: no way to erase pushed event text (and push never redacts local text)
findings.witness: Emulator: owner deleteDoc on users/alice/projects/p1/events/000000 is denied (rules line 81); push sends e as full event with raw text, no maskSecrets pass.
findings.observed: Static analysis of rules (the delete denial) plus code read; not separately executed.
findings.fix: Allow owner delete of events/projects (deleted from CLI-claimed clients only) and run maskSecrets over event text before push.

findings.title: Consent: no challenge code, substring title match forgeable, never revocable, and inherited from the log (cloned/pulled)
findings.claim: hasGeminiConsent(S)=∃ decision: title∋'gemini'∧'privacy' ∧ selected='yes'. ⇒ (a) later 'no' does not revoke, (b) any decision title containing both words grants it, (c) cws ai records a human DECISION_RECORDED after a bare 'yes' (no challenge code, contradicting spec decision rule), (d) a consent decision already in a cloned/pulled log authorises THIS user's key and data
findings.observed: RED 4/4: revocation ignored; 'Do not send anything to gemini; privacy review pending'=yes grants consent; 'yes' alone is recorded as human decision (prompt asked only 'Consent (yes/no): '); non-interactive agent run calls Gemini on a pre-existing consent decision. Combined with K-1 a remote can grant consent.
findings.fix: Store consent per user outside the log (credentials dir) or require confirmDecision() code; exact-title + latest-decision-wins; ignore consent not authored this session.

findings.title: Gemini output stored without redaction (secrets echoed by the model land in events.jsonl and later in Firestore)
findings.claim: ∃ model reply r with secret token t: after cws ai, events.jsonl contains t verbatim; ai.ts never calls maskSecrets/redactSecrets on notes, claims, proposals or summary
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/gemini.test.ts 'Gemini output is redacted before it is stored in the log' (fake caller returns ghp_ token and AKIA key)
findings.fix: Pass every output string through maskSecrets before parseEventInput, and mask on push.

findings.title: Quota counts only successful calls; counter file is agent-editable, accepts negatives and resets to 0 when corrupt
findings.claim: failed API calls and invalid-JSON replies (billed/rate-consumed) do not increment; ai-usage.json {count:-1000000} gives unlimited calls; garbage file => count 0; read-modify-write is unlocked
findings.observed: RED 4/4: failing call count stays 0; invalid JSON count stays 0; todayCount=-1000000; corrupt file => ok:true.
findings.fix: Increment before the call (reserve), validate count as non-negative int, fail closed on corrupt file, keep counter in user config dir under the lock.

findings.title: AI events appended one by one (not appendBatch): a bad item leaves a partial write and an uncounted call
findings.claim: ai.ts loops log.append per note/claim/proposal; if item k throws (e.g. status proposal on unknown claim, derivedFrom) items <k stay committed, the command exits 1, usage is not incremented, rerun repeats
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/gemini.test.ts 'is all-or-nothing' (notes n1,n2 + status proposal on c_does_not_exist)
findings.observed: RED: 'exit 1 but 2 AI events were already committed (partial write)'. Also N lock acquisitions + N full-file rereads for N items (O(n^2)); notes/claims count is uncapped.
findings.fix: Build all EventInputs, call appendBatch once, increment usage regardless of outcome; cap items.

findings.title: Login trusts the uid inside an unsigned, unverified JWT payload; the pasted token is stored as-is with no expiry or refresh
findings.claim: loginWithToken(t): uid := payload.user_id||sub from base64 of t.split('.')[1] with no signature check; refreshToken := t; no expiresAt, no refresh logic exists
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/sync.test.ts 'the uid is not taken from an unverified, unsigned JWT payload' and 'login tokens have an expiry/refresh path'
findings.observed: RED: token 'xx.<b64{sub:victim-uid}>.sig' yields creds.uid='victim-uid'; creds carry only uid/refreshToken. uid also flows unvalidated into Firestore paths (users/${uid}/...).
findings.fix: Verify the token via Firebase Auth (accounts:lookup / securetoken), derive uid from the verified response, validate uid charset, store expiry.

findings.title: Credential storage: plaintext JSON, 0600 only on creation (no-op on Windows), token accepted via argv
findings.claim: saveCredentials writes refreshToken plaintext; mode:0o600 applies only when the file is created (existing file keeps its mode) and is ignored on NTFS; `cws login --token <t>` puts the credential into shell history and the process list
findings.witness: tests/redteam/cloud/sync.test.ts 'a stored credential file that already exists with wide permissions is tightened to 0600 (POSIX)' (skipped on Windows); `cws login --token SECRET` then inspect process list / PSReadLine history.
findings.observed: Test skips on win32 (this host); finding is from code reading. Path is correctly outside the repo (%APPDATA%\cws or XDG), so not in .cws/ or logs.
findings.fix: chmod after write, icacls on Windows or use OS keychain; read token from stdin/env only; mask in errors.

findings.title: Heavy runtime dependency for an optional feature: firebase web SDK (205 prod packages, 35 MB) with a high-severity @grpc/grpc-js advisory; firebase-tools adds ~650 more
findings.claim: A local-first CLI ships `firebase` as a hard dependency; pnpm audit --prod reports 1 high (GHSA-m9gg-hp2v-232j) + 1 low via firebase>@firebase/firestore>@grpc/grpc-js <1.13.6
findings.witness: pnpm ls --prod --depth Infinity --parseable | sort -u | wc -l  (205); same without --prod (861); pnpm audit --prod
findings.observed: 205 unique prod packages, 861 incl. dev; node_modules/.pnpm 461 MB (firebase 35 MB, @google/genai 12 MB, firebase-tools 8 MB shell + deps); audit: 1 high, 1 low. Both SDKs are lazy-imported, so offline use is not slowed, but install and supply-chain surface are.
findings.invariant: new: dependency weight of optional cloud features is paid by every installer
findings.fix: Move cloud to optionalDependencies/peer or a separate package; use Firestore REST with fetch instead of the SDK; bump grpc-js override.
